script: セイバールート十四日目-111
title: セイバールート十四日目-111

pages.ja:
最後に。
もう一度、あの赤い丘を見る。
pages.jaRuby:
最後に。
もう一度、あの赤い丘を見る。
pages.en:
—One last time.

I look again upon that red hill.
pages.mirrorMoon:
At the end…
I see that red hill once more.

pages.ja:
赤い記憶。
以前より深く彼女の記憶に沈んで、同時に、これが最
後なのだと感じていた。
pages.jaRuby:
赤い記憶。
以前より深く彼女の記憶に沈んで、同時に、これが最
後なのだと感じていた。
pages.en:
A memory stained red.

I sink deeper into her memories than I ever have before, and at the same time, I know this will be the last.
pages.mirrorMoon:
A red memory.
I dive deeper into her memory, and I realize this is the last time.

pages.ja:
それはもう何度も見てきた、ある騎士の記憶。
国王となり、自分の意志を殺して国の意思となり、信
頼できる騎士たちから疎まれるようになった日々。
pages.jaRuby:
それはもう何度も見てきた、ある騎士の記憶。
国王となり、自分の意志を殺して国の意思となり、信
頼できる[ruby text="と"]騎[ruby text="も"]士たちから疎まれるようになった日々。
pages.en:
It is the memory of a certain knight, one I have seen many times now.

The days when she became king, killed her own will to become the will of the nation, and gradually came to be shunned even by the knights she had trusted.
pages.mirrorMoon:
These are the memories of a knight which I have seen many times before.
After becoming king and becoming the will of the country by killing her own will, her days were filled with neglect even from her trusted knights.

pages.ja:
戦に勝利する度に、望まぬ戦いを望まれたアルトリア。
女性である事を隠し続け、不審を買い、孤立した彼女
に待っていたものは、肉親による謀反だった。
pages.jaRuby:
戦に勝利する度に、望まぬ戦いを望まれたアルトリア。
女性である事を隠し続け、不審を買い、孤立した彼女
に待っていたものは、肉親による謀反だった。
pages.en:
Each time Artoria won a war, her people demanded another war she herself had never wanted.

She continued hiding the fact that she was a woman, invited suspicion, and became isolated. What awaited her in the end was a rebellion by one of her own blood.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Every time she won a battle, Arturia was made to wish for a battle she did not wish for.
She continued to hide her sex, surrounded by suspicion. What awaited this isolated girl was a rebellion by one of her relatives.

pages.ja:
遠征に出た王の留守を狙い、国を乗っ取った若い騎士。
男の名はモードレット。
騎士王の姉ギネヴィアの息子であるその騎士は、その
実、騎士王の息子だった。
pages.jaRuby:
遠征に出た王の留守を狙い、国を乗っ取った若い騎士。
男の名はモードレット。
騎士王の姉ギネヴィアの息子であるその騎士は、その
実、騎士王の息子だった。
pages.en:
While the king was away on campaign, a young knight seized the country in her absence.

His name was Mordred.

That knight, the son of Guinevere, the Knight King’s elder sister, was in truth the Knight King’s own son.
pages.mirrorMoon:
A young knight took over the country while the king was on an expedition.
The man’s name was Mordred.
That knight who was son of Morgan, the sister of the king of knights, was actually the son of the king of knights.

pages.ja:
結論から言えば、女性であるアルトリアに子を
作る事はできなかった。
だが、確かにモードレットはアルトリアの血を受け継
いではいたのだ。
アルトリアの姉であるギネヴィア
妹でありなが
ら王となったアルトリアを恨む彼女の妄念が、どのよう
な手を尽くしたか定かではない。
pages.jaRuby:
結論から言えば、女性であるアルトリアに子を
作る事はできなかった。
だが、確かにモードレットはアルトリアの血を受け継
いではいたのだ。
アルトリアの姉であるギネヴィア
妹でありなが
ら王となったアルトリアを恨む彼女の妄念が、どのよう
な手を尽くしたか定かではない。
pages.en:
—Strictly speaking, Artoria, being a woman, could not have fathered a child.

And yet Mordred unquestionably carried Artoria’s blood.

What means Guinevere, Artoria’s elder sister, resorted to in her obsession—her hatred of Artoria for becoming king despite being the younger sister—is impossible to know.
pages.mirrorMoon:
To start at the end, Arturia could not have children as a woman.
But Mordred certainly inherited the blood of Arturia.
Arturia’s older sister, MorganI am not sure how far she went, but she despised Arturia for becoming king even though Arturia was younger than her.

pages.ja:
彼女の分身として作られたモードレットは、父を明か
せぬ騎士として王に仕え、その座を簒奪する日を待ち、
ついに反旗を翻した。
pages.jaRuby:
彼女の分身として作られたモードレットは、父を明か
せぬ騎士として王に仕え、その座を[ruby text="さん"]簒[ruby text="だつ"]奪する日を待ち、
ついに反旗を翻した。
pages.en: Mordred, created as her double, served the king as a knight who could not reveal his father, waited for the day he could usurp the throne, and at last raised the banner of rebellion.
pages.mirrorMoon: Mordred was created as her other self. He served the king as a knight with an unknown father, waited for his chance to take over the throne, and finally organized a revolt.

pages.ja:
後にカムランの戦いと呼ばれる、
アーサー王の最期である。
pages.jaRuby:
後にカムランの戦いと呼ばれる、
アーサー王の最期である。
pages.en:
—This would later be called the Battle of Camlann.

The final battle of King Arthur.
pages.mirrorMoon:
This was the battle later known as the battle of Camlann.
The
end
final battle
of King Arthur.

pages.ja:
遠征先でモードレットの裏切りを知ったアーサー王は、
疲れ切った兵を連れて国に戻り、自らの領土へ侵攻した。
かつて従えていた騎士をことごとく斬り伏せ、
自身が守ってきた土地に攻め入った。
かろうじて自分に付き従ってくれた騎士たちも散って
いき、最後に残った者は、自身と、息子である騎士だけ
だった。
pages.jaRuby:
遠征先でモードレットの裏切りを知ったアーサー王は、

かろうじて自分に付き従ってくれた騎士たちも散って

だった。
pages.en:
King Arthur learned of Mordred’s betrayal while away on campaign. She returned to the country with her exhausted soldiers and invaded her own territory.

She cut down, one after another, the knights who had once served beneath her.

She marched into the very land she herself had protected.

Even the knights who had somehow remained loyal to her fell away, until at last only two remained: herself, and the knight who was her son—Mordred.
pages.mirrorMoon:
King Arthur discovered Mordred’s betrayal on her expedition and returned to her homeland with her tired troops to invade her own territory.
She slashed away knights that used to serve her.
She attacked the lands she once protected.
The few knights that stayed with her died off, and the only ones standing in the end were her and Mordred.

pages.ja:
両者の一騎打ちは、王の勝利で幕を下ろした。
……だが、無傷だったという訳ではない。
強い呪いでくくられたモードレットは死してなお剣を
振るい、王に、もはや癒せない傷を残したからだ。
それがこの戦いの終わり。
騎士王と言われた彼女の、最後の姿だった。
pages.jaRuby:
両者の一騎打ちは、王の勝利で幕を下ろした。
……だが、無傷だったという訳ではない。
強い呪いでくくられたモードレットは死してなお剣を
振るい、王に、もはや癒せない傷を残したからだ。
それがこの戦いの終わり。
騎士王と言われた彼女の、最後の姿だった。
pages.en:
Their duel ended in the king’s victory.

...But she did not emerge unscathed.

Bound by a powerful curse, Mordred swung his sword even after death, leaving the king with a wound that could no longer be healed.

That was the end of the battle.

The final sight of the woman they had called the Knight King.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Their personal combat ended with the king’s victory.
…But she did not emerge unscathed.
Mordred was bound by a strong curse, so he still swung his sword even after his death and left a fatal wound on the king.
That is the end of this battle.
The last of her, the one called the king of knights.

pages.ja:
辛くなかった筈はない。
思えば、彼女の戦いで辛くなかったものなどなかった。
十二もの戦はそのどれもが身を削くような戦いであり、
これは、その最後に相応しい、もっとも大きな傷痕に他
ならない。
pages.jaRuby:
辛くなかった筈はない。
思えば、彼女の戦いで辛くなかったものなどなかった。
十二もの戦はそのどれもが身を[ruby text="さ"]削くような戦いであり、
これは、その最後に相応しい、もっとも大きな傷痕に他
ならない。
pages.en:
—There is no way it did not hurt.

Come to think of it, none of her battles could ever have been anything but painful.

Each of those twelve wars had worn her away, body and soul. And this, fittingly enough, was the deepest scar of them all.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It must have been painful.
Come to think of it, none of her battles were painless.
Every one of her twelve battles was severe, and this just happened to be the greatest wound appropriate for her end.

pages.ja:
ブリテンに戻り、自国の軍を蹴散らし。
臣下であった騎士たちを自らの手で処罰し、従ってく
れた騎士たちをみな死なせ。
その果てに、カタチの上であれ、息子であった騎士を
倒さねばならなかった。
pages.jaRuby:

れた騎士たちをみな死なせ。
その果てに、カタチの上であれ、息子であった騎士を

pages.en:
She returned to Britain and crushed the army of her own country.

She personally punished the knights who had once been her subjects, watched every knight who still followed her die, and in the end was forced to strike down a knight who, in form if nothing else, had been her own son.
pages.mirrorMoon:
She returned to
Britain
her territory
and destroyed her own army.
She punished the knights who used to serve her, and the knights following her all died.
And in the end, she had to kill her own son, even if he was son only in name.

pages.ja:
……その胸に去来したものが何であるか、俺には知る
よしもない。
ただ、願ってしまった。
最期まで王として有り続けようとした独りの騎士。
その死の直前に見た夢が、せめて
アルトリアと
いう少女が望んだ、当たり前の夢であるようにと。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
...I have no way of knowing what passed through her heart then.

I can only wish.

For that lone knight who tried to remain a king until the very end.

I wish that the dream she saw just before she died was, at least, an ordinary dream—the kind the girl named Artoria herself would have wanted.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…I cannot tell what went through her mind.
But I have to wish.
The lone king, who tried to be a king until her last moments…
I wish that her last dream might be a normal dream, one that the girl called Arturia might wish for.

pages.ja:

いつのまに帰ってきたのか、自分の部屋にいて、体は

pages.en:
“Mm...”

I open my eyes.

At some point I must have been brought home. I am in my room, lying on my futon.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hm…”
I open my eyes.
I don’t know when I got back, but I’m in my room lying on my futon.

What about Saber?

Once my injuries are healed, I can manage somehow.

But Saber is different. She may be able to heal wounds, but her supply of magical energy is not infinite.

Normally, fighting would not be a problem for her. But she has just used Excalibur.

“…I see. That’s great, but…”

If my wound has healed, I’m fine.
But Saber’s different. Even though she can heal her wounds, her magical energy isn’t infinite.
It wouldn’t be a problem if she had just fought, but she used Excalibur.
She used Excalibur. She may not even have enough magical energy to heal herself.

“That is not true. Compared to you, my injuries are minor.
But I cannot ignore what you just said. Your wounds may have closed, Shirou, but they were severe enough that you could easily have died. For now, please worry about your own body.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“That is not true. I only have a light wound compared to you.
But I cannot ignore what you just said. Even if your wounds have healed, they were bad enough that you could have died. Please worry about yourself for now.”

There is a chilled towel in it. She wrings the towel out and begins wiping the sweat from my body.

pages.en:
“But at present, I am the healthier one.
Until my Master’s wounds are healed, it is only natural that I protect him.”

“—”

...What kind of answer is that?

When she says it with a face like that, I can’t argue with her anymore.

“But, I am doing better than you right now. It is only natural for me to protect you until you get better.”
“”
…What’s with that?
I can’t object if she says so with that kind of an expression.

すから」

“Of course. Even I cannot maintain myself indefinitely without sleep.”

“…Then you’ll rest once I recover, Saber?”
“Of course. I need to sleep as well.”

...And so, trying to endure my embarrassment, I let Saber continue tending to me.

セイバーはいつもの調子で、月明かりだけが彼女の体

pages.en:
“........”

...Only time passes, slowly.

Have I ever simply watched Saber this close up, without doing anything else?

She is as composed as ever, her body lit only by the moonlight.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
…Time passes slowly.
Have I ever looked so closely at Saber without doing anything?
Saber is the same as always, and moonlight is shining on her.

pages.ja:

」
……こうして見ると、セイバーは本当に女の子だった。
白い指、華奢な腕。
戦いなんて出来そうもなく、倒れれば立ち上がれそう
にないほど可憐だと思う。
……だから余計に、冷静でいられなくなる。
その細い体で、ずっと、今まで戦ってきたのだから。

pages.en:
“........”

...Looking at her like this, Saber really is just a girl.

White fingers. Slender arms.

She looks so delicate that you would never imagine her capable of fighting, so fragile that if she fell, she might never stand again.

...And that is exactly why I find it even harder to stay calm.

Because she has spent all this time fighting in that slight body.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
Looking at her now, she really is feminine.
White fingers and slender arms.
She looks so lovely that it doesn’t seem like she would be capable of fighting.
…That’s why I can’t stay calm.
She’s been fighting all this time with that slim body of hers.

pages.en:
“Shirou...? What is it? You have been staring at my arm.
...Surely you are not comparing it to Rin’s?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Shirou…? Why are you staring at my arm?
…I do not want to suspect this, but are you comparing my arms to those of Rin?”

pages.en:
...I cannot tell whether she is angry or sulking.

Her arms are so slender, and yet Saber seems convinced they are not feminine.

Maybe it is because they have muscle on them, but as far as I am concerned, they are more than cute enough.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…Is she angry or sulking?
She has such slender arms, but she thinks her arms aren’t cute at all.
Probably because there’s some muscle on them, but they’re rather cute to me.

pages.mirrorMoon: “No. The wound doesn’t hurt, so I was just spacing out. It’s not like I have anything to say about your arms.”

頷いて、

pages.en:
“I see. Then that is acceptable.”

Saber lets out a breath of relief.

Then, a moment later—

Apparently something catches in her mind. She closes her eyes, gives a small nod, and...
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see. That is good.”
Saber seems relieved.
Then…
Saber notices something as she closes her eyes and nods.

それに、貴方が助かって、本当に良かった」
嬉しそうに。
俺にとってはあまりにも儚げに、彼女は笑った。

pages.en:
“Your injuries truly are all right now, then. I was genuinely angry with you at the time, but since you survived, I will let the matter rest.

...It is late, but thank you, Shirou.

And I am truly glad that you lived.”

She smiles happily.

To me, that smile looks unbearably fragile.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“So your wound is fine now? I was seriously angry before, but I will forget about it if you are all right.
…It is rather late to say this, but I thank you, Shirou.
And I am really happy that you are safe.”
She says happily.
Then, she smiles faintly.

pages.ja:

喜びを知らず、満足な楽しみなど知らなかったクセに、
こんな事で笑うのか。

“Id—”

Something as small as that makes her smile.

...I remember the memories of hers I saw in my dream.

She never knew joy, never knew any real pleasure or contentment—and something like this is enough to make her smile?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Wha”
She’s smiling about such a thing.
…I recall her memories in my dream.
She didn’t know happiness or entertainment, but she’s going to smile about something like this?

いや。
こんなつまらない事で、自分の事でもなくて、ただ他

—No.

It is precisely because this is something so small, something that is not even about herself, that she can smile like that.

She once said it herself.

That she was happier when I was smiling.

She said it with a look of complete satisfaction.
pages.mirrorMoon:
No.
She can only smile at somebody else’s safety and not at her own happiness.
Those words from before.
That she was happier seeing me smile.
She said that with a satisfied expression.

Something in me snaps.

It really feels like I am going insane, and then—

“Sh-Shirou...!?”

—I pull Saber into my arms with all my strength.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
I’m going mad.
I really feel like I’m crazy, and…
“…! Shirou…!?”
…I hug Saber with all my strength.

I ignore her and hold Saber tighter.

She wriggles to try to free herself.
I ignore that and embrace her tighter.

But now—

There is no way I can listen to that voice.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“! Shirou, please stop…! I do not know what is going on, but this is going too far for a joke…!”
Her arms resist me.
But.
I don’t listen.

“Shirou, that is enough—!”

Saber raises an arm to strike me across the face.

And to that—

“—Enough. It’s enough. You have to start smiling for yourself.”

I squeeze every feeling I have into the words and force them out.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Shirou, please!”
Saber raises her arm to hit me.
To that…
“It’s okay. Listen, you have to smile for your own sake.”
I say so from the bottom of my heart.

pages.en:
...I understand why she clings to the Holy Grail.

But I cannot accept it.

I want Saber to know ordinary human happiness. If she never does, then something about that feels wrong.

Because if she spent her entire life fighting for everyone else—

Then she deserves to be happy for every person she made happy.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…I can understand her being focused on the Holy Grail.
But I can never approve of that.
I want her to know normal happiness. I think it’ll all be a lie if she doesn’t.
Because all this time, she’s fought for others.
So she should be as happy as the people she’s made happy.

」
pages.jaRuby:

」

Even if I was unworthy, I was entrusted with my country as its king.
I failed to fulfill that duty. I cannot be allowed this... this kind of freedom.”
